metadata.title: Why "Delve" Isn't the Watermark.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: is that odd AI word the watermark? Lands the carry-out that repetition is a habit and the watermark never repeats a favourite.
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S13 (must be the SAME composition)
metadata.one_flag: S12 — fixed-partition and topic-steered watermark families
metadata.recurring: S07 -> S08 reuse the same per-position redraw mechanism

skin_warnings: B00: palette=claude but the cold open is 'un-annotated' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk

beats.narration_text: Someone asked if that odd AI-sounding word is the watermark showing through. It isn't. Liam. Take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Shannon puppet, lab, speaks to camera, hands off

beats.note: Audio baked into media/B00.mp4 by Seedance (voice MARCUS). No mp3 for this beat.

beats.narration_text: You spot a word that sounds like a machine wrote it, and two conclusions arrive together.

production_viz.label: One word, two conclusions
production_viz.mechanic: A single word set in serif on cream. Two arrows branch from it toward two conclusion cards, arriving at the same moment.

beats.narration_text: That AI wrote this — and that the strange word is the watermark. The second one is backwards.

production_viz.label: The second conclusion, inverted
production_viz.mechanic: Both conclusions labelled. The second card flips upside down and stays inverted. Nothing else moves.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to one word: delve. In scientific writing it went up something like fifteen-fold in two years.

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — delve, climbing
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. The word 'delve' in serif on cream, with a line climbing steeply beside it across a two-year span. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S13.

beats.narration_text: So the natural read is that the mark pushes the model toward words like that, and delve is what a watermark looks like from outside.

production_viz.label: The fixed-favourite reading
production_viz.mechanic: A watermark mechanism shown nudging steadily toward one fixed word, every time. Sell the reading as reasonable.

beats.narration_text: But a watermark that always favoured the same words could be stripped with a find-and-replace.

production_viz.label: Find-and-replace kills it
production_viz.mechanic: A short list of favoured words. Each is swapped for a synonym across a passage; the mark's signal drains away to nothing.

beats.narration_text: Its whole security depends on not doing that — so it doesn't.

production_viz.label: No list to attack
production_viz.mechanic: The fixed list dissolves. In its place, preferences redrawn fresh — nothing stable left to attack.

beats.narration_text: What it actually does is redraw its preferences at every single word, from a secret key and the handful of words just before.

production_viz.label: Redrawn at every position
production_viz.mechanic: A sentence building left to right. At each position a fresh set of preferred words appears and vanishes, seeded by a key and the preceding few words.

beats.narration_text: It has no opinion about delve. It favours it here, and something else three words later.

production_viz.label: Favoured once, then not
production_viz.mechanic: The anchor word sits in the preferred set once, then is absent from the next two draws while other words take its place.

beats.narration_text: The habits are a different thing entirely, and they live somewhere else — in the model itself.

production_viz.label: Two different homes
production_viz.mechanic: Two sources drawn apart on cream: the model's weights on one side, the per-position coin flip on the other. No line between them.

beats.narration_text: Which is why they repeat: the same preferences, across documents that have nothing to do with each other.

production_viz.label: The same word, unrelated documents
production_viz.mechanic: The same word surfacing in three visibly unrelated documents — a paper, an email, a listing. Same habit, no shared context.

beats.narration_text: And they don't only come from what the model read — the training that taught it to be helpful looks to be part of it too.

production_viz.label: Traced past the corpus
production_viz.mechanic: The habit traced backward past the reading corpus to a later tuning step, which is where the trail visibly strengthens.

beats.narration_text: One flag — this clean split holds for the common kind of watermark, the one keyed to context; some schemes do deliberately fix a word list or steer toward a topic, and for those the line blurs.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ONE FLAG — two watermark families

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG — two watermark families
production_viz.mechanic: Two watermark families side by side: the left redraws each position, the right holds one fixed list. A single terracotta FLAG marker over the beat — the reel's only hedge, labelled as one.

beats.narration_text: So back to delve: in one sentence the mark may have nudged it, in the next the model reached for it on its own — same word, two different reasons, and from outside they look identical.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same word, two causes

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same word, two causes
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical — same word, same climbing line. Then two sentences appear beneath it, the word in each, a different cause traced to each. The two sentences are indistinguishable.

beats.narration_text: Telling them apart takes running the same model twice, with the mark and without, and comparing.

production_viz.label: Two runs, one comparison
production_viz.mechanic: One prompt splitting into two runs — marked and unmarked — meeting at a comparison between them. The comparison is the only place an answer appears.

beats.narration_text: So an AI-sounding word doesn't prove a watermark — you'd need that comparison, and looking at the word can't give it to you.

production_viz.label: A tell, and no proof
production_viz.mechanic: AI-SOUNDING WORD at the top; an arrow to the conclusion 'THERE IS A WATERMARK' — struck through terracotta.

beats.narration_text: And prose with no tells at all doesn't mean no watermark — the mark is spread thin across choices you'd never notice.

production_viz.label: Clean prose, still marked
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring S15: NO TELLS at the top; arrow to 'THERE IS NO WATERMARK' — struck through. Beneath, an unremarkable passage with faint marks spread evenly through it.

beats.narration_text: A word that shows up again and again is a habit, not a watermark. The watermark never picks the same favourite twice.

props.quote: A word that shows up again and again is a habit, not a watermark. The watermark never picks the same favourite twice.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take three pieces of writing you're sure a human wrote — old emails, a paper from before twenty twenty-two, something from your own archive — and count the supposed AI tells in them. Then take something you know was AI-written and count again. The human samples almost never come out at zero, and that is the whole problem with reading tells as proof. It takes about ten minutes and it's hard to un-see afterwards. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Take three pieces of writing I'm sure a human wrote — old emails, a paper from before 2022, something from my own archive. Count the supposed AI tells in them. Then take something I know was AI-written and count again.
